title: Forecasting GPU Performance for Deep Learning Training and Inference
problem: Predicting GPU performance for deep learning workloads on unseen GPU models (new GPU on existing model, or existing model on new GPU) is inaccurate with prior ML-based approaches, which attempt to predict end-to-end kernel latency directly and suffer >100% error on new model-GPU pairs.
motivation: Access to new GPU hardware is limited, making performance prediction for new model-GPU combinations essential for resource planning, model architecture decisions, and procurement.
method: NeuSight decomposes a single DL kernel prediction into smaller working sets called 'tiles' that correspond to the GPU's SM-level execution granularity. Tile-granularity predictions are made by a learned ML model, then aggregated across tiles to estimate end-to-end latency. The approach is bounded by fundamental performance laws (roofline model) and incorporates both GPU hardware parameters and software library optimizations (cuDNN, cuBLAS heuristics) to constrain the prediction space, enabling generalization to unseen GPUs by parameterizing hardware characteristics rather than encoding GPU identity.
key_novelty: Decomposing DL kernel latency prediction to tile granularity aligned with SM execution, bounding predictions via performance laws, enabling accurate cross-GPU generalization without running code on the target hardware.
contributions: NeuSight framework for GPU performance forecasting on unseen model-GPU combinations
Tile-level decomposition of kernel prediction bounded by roofline performance laws
Incorporation of GPU hardware parameters and software library optimization models
Reduction of prediction error from 121.4% (prior work) to 2.3% for GPT-3 on H100

metrics.accuracy: GPT-3 inference latency error reduced from 30.8% (SOTA) to 2.3% on H100; training error reduced from 121.4% to 2.3%
metrics.other: evaluated across diverse DL workloads and up-to-date GPUs including H100

baselines: prior ML-based GPU performance prediction frameworks
limitations: Tile decomposition assumes regular, dense compute kernels; accuracy for highly irregular or sparse workloads not discussed.
primary_theme: tile-level ML-based GPU performance forecasting for unseen hardware
